description: OpenSeesPy makes the OpenSees finite-element framework available through Python. Its maintainers publish a package branch, installation pointers and source for structural and geotechnical analyses. A modeller writes Python scripts that define elements, materials, constraints and loading, then requests static or dynamic response calculations. Coverage is the user-defined building, bridge or soil domain and loading duration; the package contains no fixed site. It can produce seismic response histories used in fragility or resilience studies. The own README says use is free for research, education and internal work, while commercial redistribution needs a separate licence under UC Regents terms. The catalogue record model-opensees covers the parent engine, but does not give the OpenSeesPy package address; an RC-FIAP draft only mentions it as a dependency. A limitation is that script access does not validate elements, input motions or regulatory assumptions. No model or Python package was executed.
